Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Sudden-onset, continuous spinning vertigo for ~2 h with nausea and tinnitus; similar brief episode 1 mo ago.  
• No focal neurologic deficits, ear pain, discharge, fever, or recent viral illness reported.  
• Past history limited to premature ovarian failure on HRT.  

Working diagnosis  
• Acute vestibular neuritis / viral labyrinthitis—most consistent with continuous vertigo, tinnitus, gait unsteadiness, and absence of focal deficits.

Differential considerations (consistent with DDx)  
• Ménière’s disease—recurrent vertigo with tinnitus; hearing loss absent, making this less likely.  
• Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)—prior short spell could fit, but current episode not positional and is prolonged.  
• Posterior-circulation (cerebellar) stroke/TIA—low-medium likelihood; needs exclusion if new neurologic signs develop.

Plan  
• Symptomatic treatment: prescribe vertigo medication (name not captured) 1 tablet TID × 10 days.  
• Arrange in-person GP assessment for otoscopy, full neurologic exam, vitals, and possible further investigations.  
• Safety-net advice: attend Emergency Department if limb weakness, severe headache, or profuse vomiting occurs.  
• Prescription sent to Lloyds Pharmacy electronically.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Vestibular neuritis / viral labyrinthitis – High likelihood: continuous spinning vertigo with tinnitus and no focal neurologic signs.  
2. Ménière’s disease – Medium likelihood: recurrent vertigo plus tinnitus but lacks hearing fluctuation.  
3. Posterior-circulation stroke/TIA – Low-medium likelihood: acute vertigo with gait unsteadiness; needs exclusion though risk factors absent.
